sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. Paradeep Parivahan is an operating logistics and port-handling company, not Paradeep Phosphates and not a port-concession proxy. It has grown service revenue at 19.08% over five years and earned respectable incremental returns, but cash realization and acquisition integration are the decisive weaknesses. FY26 parent services grew 7.80%, well below 15.03% total revenue growth; trading explains much of the difference. Parent three-year CFO/PAT is 59.45%, and first-year group CFO is only ₹1.8119 cr against PAT ₹33.5707 cr. Most importantly, an acquired subsidiary’s auditor explicitly cannot quantify gratuity and confirmation adjustments. Diagnostic BQS 5.0, GQS 5.0 after the cash ceiling, and IAS NS are not ranking-eligible. At the dated secondary ₹299.35 close, the funded conditional base yields 8.66%, below 15%; its 15% hurdle entry is ₹225.42, not a buy recommendation or executable quote. Bear funding fails, so no non-rescue bear IRR is presented.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: BSE SME 544383 / PPARIVAH / INE0SMW01011. Cutoff 20 October 2026; market reference 19 October 2026; five-year equity horizon 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031 using ACT/365.25 and 15% nominal pre-personal-tax hurdle. The illustrative position is ₹500000, not a user portfolio assumption. Exact 1,200 share lot produces one lot ₹359220 or two lots ₹718440 at ₹299.35. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold-unresolved, G3 Conditional, G4 Hold-unresolved. Financial sources are complete official annual reports, IPO restatements, subsidiary accounts and rating rationale, not an aggregator’s ratios. Indian AS accounts use parent lakhs, subsidiary thousands and this report crore. First consolidated FY26 has no prior group comparatives. Dated secondary market data is retained, but the official BSE bhavcopy request returned 403 and was not bypassed. 18 rows cover only 18 of 20 recent reference sessions and 18 of 60; gaps are not zero trades. Observed-only turnover is diagnostic, not an authenticated liquidity window. Official NSE interoperability data verifies identity/lot/shares, not an NSE listing or actual BSE surveillance clearance.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: All 13 canonical factors are explicitly assessed, with unavailable R,P,L left NS. BQS weights are GOV 20%,MOAT 20%,REV 12%,DUR 10%,CAP 12%,CASH 10%,BAL 8%,EXEC 8%; raw 4.96 and displayed 5.0. GQS weights are REV 40%,DUR 20%,EARN 15%,CAP 15%,CASH 10%; raw 5.75 is capped at 5.00 because persistent cash realization is weak and CASH 3. The cap is substantive, not hidden by rounding. IAS uses unrounded BQS 4.96 for Q, not displayed 5.0: known Q 1.24 plus D 0.80 gives 2.04; coverage 45%, missing weight 55%, mathematical range 2.59–7.54, not a point estimate or confidence interval. All rankings are excluded while G2 is unresolved, including otherwise complete BQS/GQS. Valuation does not lower BQS; cash realization and capital returns have separate economic reasons. Moving GOV and CAP one point each changes BQS by up to 0.32; differences within that range should not be overinterpreted. Compounder tests fail on business quality, moat, cash and unresolved gates, irrespective of a low headline P/E.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company loads/unloads vessels, moves cargo within ports, handles rakes, offers shore handling/stevedoring, hires equipment, transports bulk commodities and provides bagging/warehousing. It is a contractor/service operator exposed to customers’ cargo volumes, tenders, fuel, labor and fleet availability, not the owner of a uniquely scarce port franchise. FY26 group external revenue ₹418.9196 cr reconciles gross segment revenue ₹444.3222 cr less ₹25.4026 cr intersegment. Gross segments: transport ₹190.4152 cr, cargo handling ₹139.2777 cr, hiring ₹62.1501 cr, trading ₹43.6304 cr, construction ₹8.0458 cr and other ₹0.803 cr. Do not sum those as external revenue or treat segment results, which include other income, as clean recurring EBIT. Four wholly owned subsidiaries add logistics, chemical trading and related activities; real-estate stock ₹4.591 cr and unbilled WIP ₹8.206 cr broaden capital allocation risk. Revenue is earned before or after customer billing, but cash to vendors frequently precedes customer receipts by 90–120 days according to management. That working capital gap is a core business feature, not merely accounting noise.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Experience at Paradip and other ports, mechanized equipment, local execution teams and repeat industrial customers can improve turnarounds and reduce operational mistakes. Those are useful qualifications but not proof of pricing power or structural excess returns. IPO top 10 customer concentration 97.09% in FY24 and 98.58% in H1 FY25 leaves bargaining power with a few large buyers; current concentration is not disclosed. The rating highlights unionized labor, commodity cycles, port competition and competitive license/tariff structures. J M Baxi’s bulk division directly overlaps in stevedoring, mechanized bagging, inland road/rail support and warehouse services. Sical has overlapping integrated terminal/road/rail operations but different assets and capital history. IPO comparators Allcargo,Navkar and CONCOR are useful breadth checks, not pure-play port-labor/fleet peers; their rail/container/concession/scale economics prevent mechanical multiple transfer. This research uses no unverified matched-date peer median. A defensible moat upgrade would require renewals with retained price/margins, measurable utilization advantage and evidence customers cannot cheaply substitute another operator.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Six annual parent rows from FY21 through FY26 are provided. Revenue rose ₹149.3707 cr to ₹386.3058 cr, total CAGR 20.93%; services rose to ₹357.5857 cr, five-year CAGR 19.08%, the predefined REV basis. Three-year parent total CAGR 24.03% is shown as a cross-check, not selected because higher. FY25 service ₹331.7215 cr jumped from ₹211.2695 cr, whereas FY26 services grew 7.80%; goods increased ₹4.095 cr to ₹28.7201 cr. Group FY26 includes post-acquisition activity and eliminations, so ₹418.9196 cr compared to prior parent ₹335.8165 cr is not organic growth. New businesses and higher goods pass-through can lift sales without proportional fleet profit. Management’s dated ₹546 cr FY27 ambition, chemicals opportunity and October JSW ₹30 cr annual estimate remain forecasts. The December 2025 ₹593.02 cr order book is not refreshed to October 2026 or added to annual sales. Core cases use 2%/10%/16% future growth, not mechanical extrapolation of the strongest historical year.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Service growth requires equipment reliability, drivers/labor, supplier advances, customer credit, security deposits and capital goods payments. The strongest historical capital evidence is parent-only: incremental normalized NOPAT divided by additional assets before payables is 28.68% for FY22–25 and 23.85% for FY23–26 after removing identifiable acquired-share advances and subsidiary funding. Those asset proxies use NET PPE, not gross replacement cost. The latest fully reconciled net operating capital is ₹174.6999 cr versus ₹130.1495 cr, with ₹10.5931 cr incremental NOPAT, or 23.78%. High 149.78% FY22–24 net incremental ratio on one IPO restated basis is disclosed but not extrapolated because depreciation and working capital changes shrink the denominator. Current parent investments, related loan and subsidiary advances are excluded from the core bridge; old unidentified advances make earlier broad proxies conservative but imperfect. Group gross PPE ₹135.3626 cr versus net ₹40.3053 cr warns that replacement costs can exceed accounting depreciation. FY26 additions largely warehouse, not the proposed new bulker fleet. Eight-year UltraTech operations and two-year JSW contract create runway only if unit costs, minimum volumes, battery/service fees and residual values produce adequate returns. Growth financed by yet-unpaid warrants is not already funded.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The operating record and actual customer work are real positives, but related-party capital allocation needs independent scrutiny. March 31 promoter holding 65.96% is unpledged in that filed register, not an authenticated October position. FY25 ₹4.7821 cr advances went to promoter sellers before MRTC acquisition; four cash acquisitions later total ₹12.5097 cr against ₹10.6122 cr net assets. Related transport, fuel, hire and service payments are disclosed; ordinary-course/arm’s-length statements are management representations, not independent economic proof. Gloport’s ₹4.4788 cr loan including interest,12% coupon and ten-year repayment from April 2027 is nonoperating exposure, not immediate cash. FY26 secretarial/audit trail/IFC reporting is positive, parent bank returns agree, and no actual default is reported. Counterbalance: MRTC gratuity lacks actuarial provision and confirmation adjustments are unquantified. Parent confirmation emphasis is separately bounded as immaterial and must not be overstated. Execution ledger: IPO listed March 2025; acquisition cash completed August 2025 with date basis difference;45 EVs commenced June 2026 per company release; JSW contract signed October 2026 but 100 bulkers remain proposed. A cancelled Kolkata tender and early shipbuilding/fabrication ambitions are not fulfilled milestones. CFO appointment is a dated personnel change, not evidence of misconduct.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Three distinct earnings adjustments matter. First, group PBT ₹45.61 cr plus finance ₹5.4852 cr minus all other income ₹3.1108 cr gives core EBIT ₹47.9844 cr; adding disclosed deferred IPO expense ₹4.4809 cr gives normalized EBIT ₹52.4653 cr and 25% tax NOPAT ₹39.3490 cr. Gratuity reversal ₹2.2443 cr is removed with other income. Second, original FY22/23 profits change in IPO restatement because gratuity/deferred tax, and FY24 IPO tax basis differs from later annual comparative; complete bridge rows prevent treating those as organic profit. Third, FY25 finance ₹6.3098 cr becomes ₹5.9552 cr in latest comparison while other expenses rise ₹0.3546 cr; PBT unchanged, so it is a classification change, not hidden profit. Reported parent EPS 19.34 versus 21.15 uses changed weighted shares; same current-share base FY25 EPS is about ₹15.18 and FY26 ₹19.34. Cash: parent FY26 CFO ₹17.8953 cr less capex ₹13.9452 cr less finance ₹5.4532 cr is negative ₹1.5031 cr before long advances/acquisitions. Group CFO ₹1.8119 cr less capex is negative ₹12.1333 cr. Group cash flow sums reconcile, but acquisition-date cash/prior advances are not publicly bridged; implied subsidiary opening cash ₹5.8979 cr differs from subs April 1 ₹5.334324 cr. No balancing plug is invented. Inventory includes property ₹4.591 cr and unbilled cost ₹8.206 cr; receivables include unprovided-doubtful ₹5.8206 cr. Known group gratuity ₹1.8684 cr less LIC ₹0.25 cr is not exhaustive because MRTC liability is unknown. Tax disputes ₹3.6605 cr are contingent, not already due. Clean main audit does not remove these questions.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At secondary ₹299.35 close, equity value ₹476.51 cr, reported group P/E 14.19 x and normalized P/E 13.52 x are reference arithmetic, not an ordinary current signal. The sector model uses enterprise EBIT multiples 6/8/10, recurring hire/rent within margins,25% tax,2% revenue D&A, capex 6%/4.5%/4.5%, operating WC 40%/35%/33%, and dated debt/cashflow. March current cash ₹22.4698 cr is separated from ₹8.2431 cr FDs;₹0.0600184 cr IPO earmark funds only eligible WC. Opening debt ₹69.7482 cr includes ₹19.084 cr current maturities once. Identified statutory dues ₹4.9903 cr and net current tax ₹2.9191 cr are excluded from opening operating WC and paid once;₹0.5 cr gratuity is paid and known remainder ₹1.1184 cr retained at exit. Existing acquisitions, capital advances and upfront warrants are not repaid/readded. Every monthly interval is prefunded before operating receipts and minimum cash ₹8 cr tested, including before entry. Historical 45 cr revolver ceiling is conditional, not verified October headroom. Base funded IRR 8.66%, bull 23.53%; bear fails. Base hurdle entries 12/15/18% are ₹257.26/₹225.42/₹198.19. Terminal value retains cash reserve and deducts debt/gratuity; no extra property/goodwill/FD credit. Reverse growth at fixed base economics finds no funded crossing through 60% growth, so no endpoint masquerades as a solution. 27 valuation rows,48 WC/capex/reserve rows,16 fleet/warrant rows and 4 unknown-liability stresses are embedded. Separate whole-share counterfactual rescues show dilution, not committed funding.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear case is profitable book earnings combined with advance-funded contracts, aged collections, replacement costs and opaque group integration. A2% growth/8.5% EBIT margin/6% capex/40% WC case cannot maintain ₹8 cr cash floor even using the historical 45 cr credit ceiling; maximum gap ₹53.73 cr is a modeled shortfall, not a reported default. Ordinary and non-rescue returns are NS, even if an unfunded terminal calculation produces a positive price. Extra ₹25/50/75 cr fleet deployment stress confronts undisclosed EV/bulker terms; holding future contract profits without capital would be invalid. Optional September 2027 warrant cash cannot repair an earlier pre-entry breach. A separate counterfactual emergency issue before uses assumes ₹239.48 per share,20% below reference,2% fees and integer new shares; its diluted return is not the ordinary case. Unknown MRTC gratuity receives extra ₹1/3/5 cr tests, not an unsupported zero-liability conclusion. Other loss channels are goodwill impairment, property inventory recovery, major client loss, contract price/fuel mismatch and SME exit gaps. Thesis falsification is weak cash conversion continuing after collectible advances should settle, or new funding required merely to maintain reported earnings.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold share prices over the exact five-year horizon require annual appreciation 37.98% and 58.50%. The funded bull terminal ₹860.80 is only about 2.88 x reference, not 5 x. At fixed base 12.5% EBIT margin,8 x exit,35% working capital and 4.5% capex, neither 5 x nor 10 x has a funded growth solution within 0–60% annual growth. This is not proof such prices are impossible: different margins, contract structure or new capital could change outcomes. But no TAM claim, rerating alone, or 100 bulker headline establishes them. Any new share funding changes per-share ownership; optional warrants add 1.04 million shares only upon exercise. A credible multibagger case requires operating cash growth, replacement-adjusted unit returns, broader customers and cleared audited liabilities before choosing a richer terminal multiple.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Prioritize auditable clearance, not price ticks: (1) Obtain MRTC actuarial valuation and quantified confirmation/provision outcomes; zero is not a valid placeholder. (2) Reconcile acquired cash, promoter advance adjustment, acquisition-date balances and group CF classification. (3) Track parent services growth from 7.80% and separate goods/pass-through sales; require two comparable periods before REV trajectory change. (4) Track ₹5.8206 cr doubtful receivables,₹8.206 cr unbilled WIP,₹40.6092 cr supplier advances, ageing and actual cash collection. (5) Require CFO after interest/capex to turn positive without new related funding. (6) Verify current 45/53 cr facility limits, draw availability,₹19.084 cr current term repayment and deposit restrictions. (7) Obtain ownership/lease/vehicle price/battery service minimums, volume commitments and financing for 45 EVs and 100 bulkers; compare actual JSW profits against management forecast only after delivery. (8) Track September 21,2027 warrant expiry and actual cash conversion, not assumed exercise. (9) Obtain complete 20/60 BSE sessions, active SME status, current surveillance, lot and depth before any liquidity score. Refresh on next filed results, actuarial/audit clarification, funding event or material contract change. This is a research monitoring plan, not an authorized trade or automated alert.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Hold — unresolved financial reliability and tradability. Diagnostic BQS 4.96/GQS 5.00 are retained for transparency but excluded from quality rankings while G2 holds; IAS is NS and excluded from investment rankings. This is not a proven fraud/default classification, nor a claim that all reported profit is false. Parent operating history and incremental capital returns are meaningful positives, but cannot substitute for quantified group obligations. The funded conditional base misses 15% hurdle even before claiming unpriced fleet upside. A price around ₹225.42 would improve that conditional arithmetic, not clear the gates. Action category is research priority/hold for clarification, not eligible for investment consideration at present. No portfolio allocation, personalized sell instruction or tax assumption is made. A cleared audit bridge, funded contract unit economics, sustained cash conversion and complete market evidence could support reassessment; a lower quote alone would not.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Sources below identify exact issuer documents, URLs, original content hashes and reviewed statement/audit pages. Fiscal years end March 31; ordinary models use consolidated opening balances but parent history for growth/capital comparability. Money is in INR crore; parent lakhs divided by 100, subsidiary thousands divided by 10000, original FY21 rupees divided by 10000000. Facts, management estimates and analyst assumptions are separated. Historical tax/restatement and finance classification bridges are explicit, and all model rows are embedded. No raw filing, shareholder list or personal tax identifier is part of the portable financial extract. Open questions remain MRTC actuarial/confirmation liabilities, acquired cash/prior advances, supplier advance collectibility, exact unrestricted FDs, current bank availability, fleet ownership/lease battery fees, JSW minimum volumes, promoter October ownership and full tradability. Fresh primary evidence is required to clear those questions; deterministic reconstruction of calculations is not new authentication of missing facts. The FY26 audited cash date is almost seven months before market reference, and the conditional cash bridge is not represented as an actual October bank statement.

evidence.claim: FY26 parent revenue ₹386.3058 cr increased 15.03%, but services ₹357.5857 cr grew 7.80%; goods ₹28.7201 cr versus ₹4.095 cr explains ₹24.6251 cr of ₹50.4893 cr growth.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: First consolidated revenue ₹418.9196 cr cannot be compared with parent-only historical revenue as organic growth.

evidence.claim: Comparable five-year parent service CAGR 19.08% anchors REV 7; parent total CAGR 20.93% and three-year total 24.03% are disclosed but not chosen to inflate the score.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Historical FY21–24 revenues are predominantly service revenue; no audited physical-tonnage or price/mix decomposition. No current-trajectory uplift from one period.

evidence.claim: IPO disclosed top 10 customers 97.09% of FY24 revenue and 98.58% in H1 FY25. Repeat industrial clients and port execution skills support relationships, not demonstrated pricing power.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Concentration is historical; FY26 named customer mix and contract-level margin are not disclosed. No unsupported current percentage.

evidence.claim: FY26 parent and consolidated main opinions and actual IFC annexures are unmodified; parent CARO bank returns agree, no default reported and audit trail is positive.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Clean headings do not remove emphases or establish liability completeness in subsidiaries.

evidence.claim: MRTC auditor explicitly says gratuity is payment-basis, not actuarially provided, with actual liability unascertainable; missing balance confirmations leave adjustments unquantified.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Opinion remains unmodified. Parent auditor separately regards remaining parent confirmations as immaterial; that does not resolve MRTC exposure.

evidence.claim: FY25 acquisition advances ₹4.7821 cr were paid to promoter sellers. FY26 four subsidiaries acquired 100% for ₹12.5097 cr cash versus net assets ₹10.6122 cr, goodwill ₹1.8975 cr.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Board August 8 versus auditor August 20 dates differ; public acquired-cash/prior-advance settlement bridge is incomplete. Not evidence by itself of fraud.

evidence.claim: Group CFS opening cash ₹61.2128 cr implies ₹5.8979 cr above parent opening cash, while subsidiaries April 1 cash totals ₹5.334324 cr. Ending group-parent cash ₹5.8535 cr reconciles subsidiary ending cash.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Difference ₹0.563576 cr may be acquisition-date scope; no explicit acquisition-net-of-cash line is shown. Do not invent a balancing correction or call it an arithmetic cash imbalance.

evidence.claim: Reported group FY26 PAT ₹33.5707 cr versus CFO ₹1.8119 cr; parent PAT ₹30.7921 cr versus CFO ₹17.8953 cr. Parent FY24–26 CFO/PAT ratio of sums is 59.45%.

evidence.claim: FY26 other income includes gratuity reversal ₹2.2443 cr; deferred IPO costs ₹4.4809 cr are expensed. Normalized group EBIT ₹52.4653 cr excludes all other income and adds only the IPO expense.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Do not add the expense back to cash again: opening deferred asset ₹4.1177 cr already unwinds through other-asset cashflow. Recurring hire, wages, fuel and rent remain.

evidence.claim: Group receivables ₹92.6166 cr include ₹5.8206 cr classified doubtful without an identified deducted allowance; parent over-three-year doubtful ₹4.7986 cr persists. Supplier advances ₹40.6092 cr and WIP ₹8.206 cr absorb cash.
evidence.counterevidence_or_limit: Classification is not proof of realized loss; negotiations and good balances provide counterevidence. Base assumes half doubtful old collections fail, stressfull, not a proven writeoff.

evidence.claim: Parent incremental NOPAT/assets-before-payables proxy returns 28.68% FY22–25 and 23.85% FY23–26 after identifiable acquisition/subsidiary funding exclusions; latest net-operating-capital bridge 23.78%.

evidence.claim: FY26 group gross PPE ₹135.3626 cr, accumulated depreciation ₹95.0573 cr, net ₹40.3053 cr; additions ₹13.9619 cr largely warehouse ₹13.1033 cr, not a major new-truck fleet.

evidence.claim: Audited group cash ₹30.7128 cr comprises current bank/cash ₹22.4698 cr and deposits ₹8.2431 cr. Total debt ₹69.7482 cr already includes ₹19.084 cr current term maturities.

summary: Hold — unresolved. Paradeep Parivahan is an operating logistics and port-handling company, not Paradeep Phosphates and not a port-concession proxy. It has grown service revenue at 19.08% over five years and earned respectable incremental returns, but cash realization and acquisition integration are the decisive weaknesses. FY26 parent services grew 7.80%, well below 15.03% total revenue growth; trading explains much of the difference. Parent three-year CFO/PAT is 59.45%, and first-year group CFO is only ₹1.8119 cr against PAT ₹33.5707 cr. Most importantly, an acquired subsidiary’s auditor explicitly cannot quantify gratuity and confirmation adjustments. Diagnostic BQS 5.0, GQS 5.0 after the cash ceiling, and IAS NS are not ranking-eligible. At the dated secondary ₹299.35 close, the funded conditional base yields 8.66%, below 15%; its 15% hurdle entry is ₹225.42, not a buy recommendation or executable quote. Bear funding fails, so no non-rescue bear IRR is presented.
